items.item_text: Bachelor’s degree and/or equivalent combination of education and experience
5 years minimum of Business operations and/or administration experience

The Department of Pediatrics is seeking an enthusiastic, organized, detail-oriented, resourceful, and collaborative professional to provide administrative and analytical support to the Department’s Vice Chair leadership team. This position will support Vice Chairs across key mission areas, including research, clinical affairs, education, academic affairs, research workforce development, community partnerships and advocacy, and innovation and strategy. The role will help ensure priorities, meetings, reports, action items, and follow-up activities are well coordinated across these leadership portfolios. Under general direction, the Executive Assistant will perform a variety of professional administrative and analytical duties, including reviewing reports, synthesizing information and data, preparing written summaries and recommendations, coordinating special projects, tracking deadlines, and supporting department-wide initiatives. Assignments may involve operational, academic, clinical, research, or financial topics with departmental or cross-departmental impact. The ideal candidate will be highly organized, responsive, and comfortable working with senior faculty and administrative leaders. This role requires strong writing skills, sound judgment, discretion, attention to detail, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a busy academic medicine environment. This is a hybrid position requiring work four days per week on-site and one day per week remote, with the remote day assigned based on departmental operational needs.
Advanced Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint)
Ability to use high-level discretion and maintain a high level of confidentiality
Knowledge of academic and/or administrative structure of institutions of higher education
Analytical skills sufficient to interpret and apply University and campus policies; define problems; formulate logical conclusions, recognize alternatives
Strong written skills to prepare accurate, concise, and clear reports and documents
Communication and interpersonal skills are sufficient to work effectively with University-wide and campus-wide Administrators, Deans, Department Chair, faculty and staff both orally and written
